# homeassistant_scheduler_schedule (Resource)

A schedule of the Scheduler integration (`scheduler`), the backend of the scheduler card: on the chosen days, it runs actions at fixed times or relative to the sun, e.g. a weekly heating plan. The Scheduler integration is a custom integration (https://github.com/nielsfaber/scheduler-component, version 3.3, e.g. installed through HACS) and must be installed and set up in Home Assistant; without it, this resource fails with an error that says so, and everything else keeps working. Changes update the schedule in place, except a new `name`, which replaces it. Edits made in the card show up as drift.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Needs the Scheduler integration (scheduler-component, e.g. from HACS) in Home Assistant.

# A weekly heating plan for one room: warm in the morning and evening on workdays.
resource "homeassistant_scheduler_schedule" "office_heating" {
  name     = "Office heating"
  weekdays = ["workday"]
  tags     = ["heating"]
  timeslots = [
    {
      start   = "06:30:00"
      stop    = "08:00:00"
      actions = [{ action = "climate.set_temperature", entity_id = "climate.office", data = jsonencode({ temperature = 21 }) }]
    },
    {
      start   = "08:00:00"
      stop    = "17:00:00"
      actions = [{ action = "climate.set_temperature", entity_id = "climate.office", data = jsonencode({ temperature = 17 }) }]
    },
  ]
}

# Lights on half an hour before sunset, unless the room is bright enough.
resource "homeassistant_scheduler_schedule" "porch_light" {
  name = "Porch light"
  timeslots = [{
    start          = "sunset-00:30:00"
    condition_type = "and"
    conditions     = [{ entity_id = "sensor.porch_illuminance", match_type = "below", value = "50" }]
    actions        = [{ action = "light.turn_on", entity_id = "light.porch" }]
  }]

  # Enforce that the schedule stays switched on. Leave it unset to manage the switch in Home Assistant.
  enabled = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the schedule. The switch's entity ID is derived from it. Changing it replaces the schedule, with a new `schedule_id`: Scheduler 3.3 loses the switch of a schedule renamed in place.
- `timeslots` (Attributes List) When the schedule runs and what it does: at a time (`start` only), or in a time range (`start` and `stop`), whose actions run at the start, and again when Home Assistant starts within the range. Timeslots with fixed times must not overlap. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeslots))

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the schedule is enabled, i.e. its switch is on. Unset, the provider neither changes nor reads it, so turning the switch on and off in Home Assistant is no drift. Set, it is enforced (ADR-0031). A `pause` schedule turns itself off after it ran, so `enabled = true` turns it on again on the next apply.
- `end_date` (String) Last day on which the schedule runs, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, not before `start_date`. Unset, it does not end.
- `repeat_type` (String) What happens after the last timeslot of a day: `repeat` (run again next time) or `pause` (turn the switch off; it must be turned on again). Defaults to `repeat`. The integration's `single`, which deletes the schedule after it ran, is not supported: the next apply would create it again.
- `start_date` (String) First day on which the schedule runs, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Unset, it starts right away.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags of the schedule, which the card filters by. Defaults to none.
- `weekdays` (List of String) Days on which the schedule runs: any of `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat`, `sun`, or `daily`, `workday`, `weekend`. `workday` follows `binary_sensor.workday_sensor`. Defaults to `["daily"]`.

### Read-Only

- `entity_id` (String) Entity ID of the schedule's switch, `switch.schedule_<name as slug>`. Turning it off disables the schedule.
- `schedule_id` (String) ID that the integration assigned to the schedule (6 hex digits). Import with this ID.

<a id="nestedatt--timeslots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeslots`

Required:

- `actions` (Attributes List) Actions to run, in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeslots--actions))
- `start` (String) Start, as `HH:MM:SS` (24 hours, e.g. `06:30:00`), or relative to the sun as `sunrise` or `sunset`, `+` or `-`, and an offset `HH:MM:SS` (e.g. `sunset-00:30:00`).

Optional:

- `condition_type` (String) How the conditions combine: `and` (all must hold) or `or` (one must hold). Unset, the integration uses `or`.
- `conditions` (Attributes List) Conditions on the state of entities that must hold for the actions to run. The card gives every timeslot the same conditions. Defaults to none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeslots--conditions))
- `stop` (String) End of the range, in the format of `start`. `00:00:00` is the end of the day. Unset, the timeslot is a single time.
- `track_conditions` (Boolean) Whether to run the actions later in the range, when the conditions start to hold. Defaults to `false`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeslots--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeslots.actions`

Required:

- `action` (String) Action to call, as `<domain>.<action>`, e.g. `climate.set_temperature`.

Optional:

- `data` (String) Data of the action, as a JSON object, e.g. `jsonencode({ temperature = 21 })`. The order of keys and the spelling of numbers do not matter. Defaults to `{}`.
- `entity_id` (String) Entity to call the action on. Unset, the action gets no target.


<a id="nestedatt--timeslots--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeslots.conditions`

Required:

- `entity_id` (String) Entity whose state is compared.
- `match_type` (String) Comparison: `is`, `not`, `below`, or `above`.
- `value` (String) Value to compare with, e.g. `on` or `20`. With `below` and `above`, it must be a number.

Optional:

- `attribute` (String) Attribute to compare instead of the state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a schedule by its schedule_id, e.g. from the homeassistant_scheduler_schedules data source.
tofu import homeassistant_scheduler_schedule.office_heating 3d22e6
```
